solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Captain finally catches fish

indicators.note: finally means only the closing letter of the word catches is used

parts.note: a kipper is a smoked herring, a fish

explanation.surface: A ship's captain at last lands a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A skipper is the master of a boat or ship, so a synonym for its captain.

clue.text: Resume novel — gripping page is outstanding

indicators.note: gripping means the shuffled letters hold the page letter inside
novel means new, so the letters of resume take a fresh order

explanation.surface: A new novel's summary, with a gripping page, is excellent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' rearranges RESUME to SUREME, which grips P.
explanation.definitionFit: Supreme means best of all, so outstanding.

clue.text: Evening out — or in, with gin

indicators.note: out means the letters are put out of place and rearranged

explanation.surface: Should you stay in or go out for an evening with gin?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Evening out' reads as a night on the town, but 'Evening' (making even) is the definition and 'out' the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Ironing makes cloth smooth and flat, so it is a way of evening it.

clue.text: Biggles, possibly, is initially captured in story

indicators.note: captured in places that letter inside the word for story

parts.note: a plot is the story of a book or film

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of is

explanation.surface: The fictional hero Biggles is captured in a tale.
explanation.walkthrough: Biggles is the flying ace of W E Johns's British boys' adventure books.
explanation.definitionFit: Biggles is a famous fictional airman, so he is an example of one who flies planes.

clue.text: Giving someone a cue, tending to follow last bits of snooker game

indicators.note: to follow puts the word for tending after those two letters
last bits of takes the final letter of each of snooker and game

parts.note: minding means tending or looking after

explanation.surface: A coach prompts a player in the closing stages of a snooker match.
explanation.definitionFit: Reminding someone gives them a prompt, as a cue does an actor.

clue.text: Rustic worker's after vegetables

indicators.note: after places the worker behind the vegetables in the answer

parts.note: peas are vegetables
an ant is the classic crossword worker, from the worker ants of a colony

explanation.surface: A farmhand is chasing after vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: A rustic, as a noun, is a country dweller; a peasant is a poor farming countryman.

clue.text: Share food caught by European

parts.note: a pie is a dish of food
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A European grabs a portion of food.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece is a portion or share of something.

clue.text: Duet? Sit at different positions

indicators.note: different means the letters are put in a different order

explanation.surface: Two singers in a duet are told to sit in different places.
explanation.definitionFit: Attitudes are postures or poses of the body, so positions.

clue.text: Camera shot capturing one's country

indicators.note: capturing means the rearranged letters hold the letter for one
shot means broken up, so the letters of camera are rearranged

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A camera shot captures a nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' rearranges CAMERA to AMERCA, which captures I.
explanation.definitionFit: America is a country, the United States.

clue.text: Mad Hatter with Alice ultimately creating drama

indicators.note: mad means crazy, so the letters of hatter are rearranged
ultimately takes the final letter of Alice

explanation.surface: The Mad Hatter with Alice puts on a show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mad' rearranges HATTER to THEATR; the E of Alice ends it.
explanation.definitionFit: Theatre is drama as an art form or the dramatic profession.

clue.text: Nuisance for the French, getting caught by leaders of British Marines

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of

indicators.note: getting caught by means the French article is held inside the following letters
leaders of takes the first letter of each of the words British and Marines

parts.note: le is the French masculine word for the

explanation.surface: A Frenchman is nabbed by British Marines, causing trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: A problem is a source of trouble, which is what a nuisance is.

clue.text: Eccentric former lover, male, hiding in box, for example?

parts.note: an ex is a former partner

indicators.note: hiding in puts the male letter inside the tree

parts.note: box is a kind of evergreen tree

explanation.surface: An odd ex-boyfriend hides inside a box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'box' looks like a container, but it is the shrub or tree, signalled by 'for example?'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something far from the normal or moderate; an extreme view is an eccentric one.

clue.text: Sixteen reforms before Church of England's survival

indicators.note: before sets the shuffled letters in front of the church abbreviation
reforms means the letters of sixteen are formed again in a new order

parts.note: CE is the abbreviation for Church of England

explanation.surface: Sixteen reforms are passed before the Church of England can survive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Church of England' is the established church in England, routinely shortened to its initials in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Survival is continued being, which is what existence means.

clue.text: Maybe Oliver Stone's beginning to be taken in by fool

indicators.note: to be taken in by puts that letter inside the word for a fool

parts.note: a twit is a fool

indicators.note: beginning means only the opening letter of Stone's is used

explanation.surface: Perhaps Oliver Stone is fooled at the start of a project.
explanation.walkthrough: Oliver Stone the film director is a red herring; Oliver Twist is the Dickens hero.
explanation.definitionFit: Oliver Twist is Dickens's orphan hero, so the surname is defined by an example bearer.

clue.text: Each golfer, oddly, gets a good score

indicators.note: oddly takes the first, third and fifth letters of golfer

explanation.surface: Every golfer, strangely enough, makes a fine score.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf an eagle is two strokes under par on a hole, a very good score.

clue.text: Busy? Drink up, bishop, and preach

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word for drink is read from bottom to top

parts.note: ale is a drink, beer
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
to orate is to speak in a lofty way, to preach

explanation.surface: A busy bishop knocks back a drink and gives a sermon.
explanation.definitionFit: A busy design is fussy and over-detailed, so elaborate.

clue.text: Urgent — I'm to intercede

parts.note: taken as written, without the apostrophe
to mediate is to intercede between parties

explanation.surface: Someone says they must step in at once.
explanation.definitionFit: Immediate means needing action now, the same sense as urgent.

clue.text: Disorder is endemic — these may help

indicators.note: disorder means the letters of is endemic are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: A widespread illness is present, and drugs may help.
explanation.definitionFit: Medicines are remedies, things that help the sick to recover.

clue.text: Returned cross after European caught and executed

indicators.note: after puts the cross mark behind the European letter

parts.note: a cross is the letter X
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
hanged means executed on the gallows

explanation.surface: An angry European is caught and put to death.
explanation.definitionFit: Exchanged goods are taken back to the shop for others, so returned in the swapping sense.

clue.text: Passage from book's absolutely correct about leaders in Telegraph, recently

indicators.note: about means the word for correct goes round the two leading letters

parts.note: exact means absolutely correct

indicators.note: leaders in takes the first letters of Telegraph and recently

explanation.surface: A book excerpt is perfectly accurate according to recent Telegraph leaders.
explanation.definitionFit: An extract is a passage taken from a book.

clue.text: Liberal stays out of entire conflict

indicators.note: stays out of means the Liberal letter is removed from the word for entire

parts.note: complete means entire, whole

explanation.surface: A Liberal stays out of an all-out war.
explanation.definitionFit: To compete is to vie or struggle against others, so conflict as a verb.

clue.text: Bank books might be here

definitions.meaning: a bookshelf is where books are stored

explanation.definitionFit: A shelf is both a raised ledge under the sea and a board on which books sit.

clue.text: Look at main turns in river

indicators.note: in puts the rearranged letters inside the river's name

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, south-west England

indicators.note: turns means the letters of main are turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone studies the main bends of a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The river Exe flows through Exeter in Devon, south-west England; 'turns' reads as bends of the river but shuffles the word main.
explanation.definitionFit: To examine is to inspect, to look at closely.

clue.text: Panic — class A drug's found inside shipment

indicators.note: found inside places the drug letter within the word for panic

parts.note: fright means sudden panic
E is short for ecstasy, a class A drug in UK law

explanation.surface: Alarm as hard drugs are discovered in a cargo.
explanation.definitionFit: Freight is goods carried by ship or vehicle, a shipment.

clue.text: Measure length of totem pole

indicators.note: length of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone measures how tall a totem pole is.
explanation.definitionFit: In music a measure can mean the rhythm or time of a piece, its tempo.

clue.text: Incite blow almost in anger

indicators.note: in places the shortened blow inside the verb for anger

parts.note: to enrage is to anger

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the word for a blow is dropped

parts.note: a coup is a sudden stroke or blow

explanation.surface: Someone stirs up trouble by nearly hitting out in a rage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blow' suggests a punch, but here it is the sudden stroke of a coup, cut short by 'almost' and put 'in' the verb meaning anger.
explanation.definitionFit: To encourage someone is to urge them on, the sense of incite.

clue.text: Blades in tents? Pointless

indicators.note: pointless means the tip, the leading letter, is cut off the word for tents

parts.note: tepees are conical Native American tents

explanation.surface: Swords are kept in tents, but it is futile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pointless' looks like a comment on futility but removes the point, the T at the front of TEPEES.
explanation.definitionFit: Epees are fencing swords, blades used in the sport.

clue.text: Advises wash, head to toe

indicators.note: head to toe means the first letter is moved to the bottom, the end

parts.note: a surge is a rush or wash of water

explanation.surface: Someone recommends a full wash from head to toe.
explanation.definitionFit: To urge someone is to press them to act, so advises.

clue.text: Lady in mature years is mean

indicators.note: in puts the lady's name inside the word for years

parts.note: age means old age, mature years
Vera is a woman's name

explanation.surface: An older woman is described as unkind.
explanation.definitionFit: In arithmetic the mean is the average of a set of values.

clue.text: Finding fault with trap, German led by horse

indicators.note: led by puts the horse first, ahead of the trap and German

parts.note: a nag is an old horse
a gin is a snare or trap

explanation.surface: A carping critic complains about a pony and trap driven by a German.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trap' suggests a pony and trap, but here it is a gin, a snare.
explanation.definitionFit: Nagging is constant criticism, so a fault-finding activity.

clue.text: Hesitates to disturb setter penning clue at last

indicators.note: penning means the shuffled letters enclose another letter, as a pen holds
to disturb means the letters of setter are thrown into a new order
at last takes the final letter of clue

explanation.surface: Someone dithers about interrupting a crossword compiler writing a clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to disturb' rearranges SETTER to TETERS, which pens E, the end of 'clue'.
explanation.definitionFit: To teeter is to waver or vacillate, so it means hesitates.

clue.text: Fancy cups set out

indicators.note: out means the letters are put out of their order

explanation.surface: Elegant cups are laid out.
explanation.definitionFit: To fancy something can mean to suspect or imagine it is so.
